1. \(x + y \equiv 0 \pmod{p}\)
2. \(x^2 - xy + y^2 \equiv 3xy - 1 \pmod{p}\)

### Case 1: \(x + y \equiv 0 \pmod{p}\)
If \(x + y \equiv 0 \pmod{p}\), then \(y \equiv -x \pmod{p}\). This means that for each \(x\), there is exactly one corresponding \(y\) (i.e., \(y = -x \mod p\)).
